newsitem.title: USA: Conn says 30 pct of welfare parents got jobs - paper.
newsitem.headline: Conn says 30 pct of welfare parents got jobs - paper.

text.p: Connecticut has doubled the numer of welfare parents with jobs in a 12-month period to 16,656, the Hartford Courant said Sunday.
As a result, 30 percent of the state's total caseload had full- or part-time jobs as of August 1996, up from 8,507 in the year-ago period.

Connecticut's program, which resembles the new federal plan's approach, limits recipients to 21 months of cash benefits. Individuals still can collect full benefits if they earn less than the federal povery line, which now is $12,980 for a family of three, the paper said.
Connecticut Gov. John Rowland was quoted as saying "We've built a good bridge--it's holding up. It is the best welfare reform plan in the country.

However, critics said the early results do not prove the effort to move people from welfare to jobs is working, saying it will take years to see the full results. Among other issues, they questioned whether the former welfare recipients would find jobs that pay enough to support their famililes.
